cut_items.item: Explicit note that the prune command removes unused networks, build cache (stated plainly), and a single-command-first approach with -f to skip prompt after stopping containers
Advice to back up needed data before deleting volumes
Fallback command `docker volume prune -a -f` if named volumes remain
Note that individual remove commands print an error on empty lists, which is harmless
Stop step comes first so prune also removes the containers (docker stop $(docker ps -q))
Provides `docker volume prune -a -f` as a follow-up to remove remaining volumes if prune left some behind
Advises backing up anything needed before deleting
Notes that empty-list errors from the per-type removal commands are harmless
Suggests running `docker system df` before and after to measure freed space
Presents per-type removal (containers, images, volumes) as separate alternative commands with labels
Concise ordering: stop running containers first, then prune in one go

added_items.item: Suggests inspecting volumes with `docker volume ls` before deleting
Step to remove all containers with `docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq)` in a numbered flow (X also lists it as an alternative)
Explains that `-a` is needed with `--volumes` to remove named volumes, in Docker 23+ (version number differs from X's 25)
Suggests checking volumes with `docker volume ls` before deleting
Explicit step to stop all containers including stopped ones via `docker stop $(docker ps -aq)`
Notes that prune also removes the unused networks, which is stated alongside the step to clear leftover networks and build cache after manual removal
Gives the simple single prune command without stopping containers first, for removing only unused resources (non-destructive to running containers)
Clarifies that with --volumes (Docker 23+), only anonymous volumes are removed unless -a is added, which also removes unused named volumes (note: version attribution differs from Y)
